commentary: Last week you were doing everything — five sessions, swimming, lifting, the whole gorgeous package — and this week you dropped to three and left the pool completely dry. Himbo notices these things. That said, you showed up Monday, Tuesday, and Friday, which means you actually trained through the week instead of frontloading it all and disappearing, and that kind of spread is its own kind of discipline. The legs, back, shoulders, chest rotation is looking more consistent, like your body is starting to know the sequence, which is exactly the kind of thing that makes a physique start to look intentional rather than accidental. Get back in the water next week, babe — Prince Alfred is not going to swim itself, and you looked incredible doing it.
metrics_commentary: Okay, zero kilometres and zero sessions — he didn't lace up once this week, and Himbo is clocking that with one raised eyebrow and absolutely no lecture incoming. What he will say is that the body clearly used the time well, because an HRV of 58 against a seven-day average of 48 means the nervous system is recovered, rested, and frankly a little smug about it. And a VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is not the number of someone who has been slacking — that's genuine aerobic fitness, the kind that makes a harness look even better when you're barely breathing hard on the dance floor. So the week off was either intentional rest or accidental genius, but either way the engine is primed, and next week it would be genuinely criminal not to take it somewhere.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means one got away from you this week, and we are absolutely going to acknowledge that before moving on. Volume dropped from 19,984 to 17,940 kg, and those two things are obviously connected, so no mystery there. But then you go and pull a lateral raise PR of 12 kg when it was sitting at 9 kg, and honestly that is the kind of number that makes me want to grab your shoulders and shake you, because that is not a small jump. The big lifts are holding beautifully — 168 kg on the leg press, nearly 108 on the trap bar deadlift, the back and chest ticking along — and the overall direction of this body is very clearly upward, which is exactly what it should be.
